name.description: A string to identify your config.

context.description: Relative path relative to the workspace root folder.

defaultProfile.description: Profile name you want to set as default.

remote.description: Name of remote which configs with `remoteFs.remote` in User Setting. Configuration will get merged to this remote.

uploadOnSave.description: Upload on every save. With profiles this is per-profile: a profile uses its own value or inherits this base one, and a save uploads to EVERY profile whose effective value is true (so a base true reaches every profile — a fleet of mirrors; set a profile's uploadOnSave to false to skip it).

useTempFile.description: Stage each upload/download into a unique temp file beside the target and atomically rename it into place, so an interrupted transfer never truncates the existing file. Falls back to a direct write when the target directory isn't writable. Set to false to force a direct overwrite. Default: true.

openSsh.description: True to enable atomic file uploads (only supported by openSSH servers). if true, `useTempFile` must also be set to true.

filePerm.description: Octal permission applied to uploaded files (e.g. 644). Leave unset to preserve the source file mode.

dirPerm.description: Octal permission applied to created remote directories (e.g. 755).

passive.description: FTP only: use passive mode for data connections.

downloadOnOpen.description: When you open a local file that also exists on the server, download the server copy over it: true (always), "confirm" (ask first), or false. Files that don't exist on the server are left alone.

syncOption.description: Behaviour of the `Sync` command. `source` and `destination` depend on direction: `Sync Local -> Remote` makes your computer the source and the server the destination; `Sync Remote -> Local` is the reverse.

delete.description: Delete files in the destination that don't exist in the source (mirror the source). Off unless set.

skipCreate.description: Don't create files in the destination that exist only in the source. Off unless set.

ignoreExisting.description: Don't touch files that already exist in the destination. Off unless set.

update.description: Overwrite an existing destination file only when the source copy is newer. Off unless set.

ignore.description: Files to skip in EVERY transfer — upload, download and sync (not deleted, just never transferred). gitignore-style patterns, matched relative to `context` for local files and to `remotePath` on the server.

ignoreFile.description: Also read ignore patterns from this file (.gitignore format, one per line); they are added to `ignore`. Path relative to the workspace root folder, or absolute. Not read unless you set it explicitly.

remoteExplorer.description: Affects ONLY how the Remote Explorer panel looks, not file transfers.

filesExclude.description: Hide these files/folders in the server tree (visual only — does not affect upload/download). gitignore-style patterns, matched relative to `remotePath`. .git/.svn/.hg/CVS/.DS_Store are always hidden too.

order.description: This server's position in the tree when several are configured: lower number sorts higher; equal values sort by name. No effect with a single server.

remoteTimeOffsetInHours.description: The number of hours difference between the local machine and remote/server. (remote minus local)

limitOpenFilesOnRemote.description: Limit the open file descriptors to the specific number in a remote server. Set to true for using default limit(222). Do not set this unless you have to.

maxFileSize.description: Skip files larger than this size (in megabytes) during batch transfers (folder upload/download/sync). A single explicit file transfer is never skipped. Omit or set to 0 to disable.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the server.

password.description: Password for password-based user authentication. Special values: "secretStorage" stores/reads the password in the OS keychain (no plaintext here); "prompt" always asks and never stores. Leave "" to be prompted (legacy behaviour).

connectTimeout.description: How long (in milliseconds) to wait for the connect to complete.

agent.description: Path to ssh-agent's UNIX socket for ssh-agent-based user authentication.  Windows users: set to 'pageant' for authenticating with Pageant or (actual) path to a cygwin "UNIX socket".

privateKeyPath.description: Absolute path to user private key.

passphrase.description: For an encrypted private key, this is the passphrase string used to decrypt it. Set to true to be prompted instead of storing it here. Set to "secretStorage" to store/read it in the OS keychain. Either way avoids a cleartext passphrase in this config.

oneOf.description: Array of predefined phrases to automatically pass them without user prompting.

interactiveAuth.description: Keyboard interaction authentication mechanism. For example using Google Authentication.

algorithms.description: Explicit overrides for the default transport layer algorithms used for the connection.

kex.description: Key exchange algorithms. Either an exact list, or an object with "append"/"prepend"/"remove" to modify the defaults (e.g. { "append": ["diffie-hellman-group1-sha1"] } to reach a legacy server).

cipher.description: Ciphers. Either an exact list, or an object with "append"/"prepend"/"remove" to modify the defaults.

serverHostKey.description: Server host key formats. Either an exact list, or an object with "append"/"prepend"/"remove" to modify the defaults.

hmac.description: (H)MAC algorithms. Either an exact list, or an object with "append"/"prepend"/"remove" to modify the defaults.

sshConfigPath.description: Absolute path to your SSH configuration file (eg. ~/.ssh/config)

sshCustomParams.description: Extra parameters append to SSH command using by "Open SSH in Terminal"

secure.description:
Set to true for both control and data connection encryption, 'control' for control connection encryption only, or 'implicit' for
implicitly encrypted control connection (this mode is deprecated in modern times, but usually uses port 990).

secureOptions.description: Options to be passed to tls.connect(). Default: (none)

host.description: Host the client should connect to, defaults to 'localhost'.

port.description: Port the client should connect to.

path.description: Creates unix socket connection to path. If this option is specified, host and port are ignored.

rejectUnauthorized.description: If true, the server certificate is verified against the list of supplied CAs. An 'error' event is emitted if verification fails; err.code contains the OpenSSL error code. Defaults to true.

NPNProtocols.description: An array of strings or Buffers containing supported NPN protocols. Buffers should have the format [len][name][len][name]... e.g. 0x05hello0x05world, where the first byte is the length of the next protocol name. Passing an array is usually much simpler, e.g. ['hello', 'world'].

ALPNProtocols.description: An array of strings or Buffers containing the supported ALPN protocols. Buffers should have the format [len][name][len][name]... e.g. 0x05hello0x05world, where the first byte is the length of the next protocol name. Passing an array is usually much simpler: ['hello', 'world'].)

servername.description: Server name for the SNI (Server Name Indication) TLS extension.

minDHSize.description: Minimum size of the DH parameter in bits to accept a TLS connection. When a server offers a DH parameter with a size less than minDHSize, the TLS connection is destroyed and an error is thrown. Defaults to 1024.

pfx.description: Optional PFX or PKCS12 encoded private key and certificate chain. pfx is an alternative to providing key and cert individually. PFX is usually encrypted, if it is, passphrase will be used to decrypt it.

key.description: Optional private keys in PEM format. PEM allows the option of private keys being encrypted. Encrypted keys will be decrypted with options.passphrase. Multiple keys using different algorithms can be provided either as an array of unencrypted key strings or buffers, or an array of objects in the form {pem: <string|buffer>[, passphrase: <string>]}. The object form can only occur in an array. object.passphrase is optional. Encrypted keys will be decrypted with object.passphrase if provided, or options.passphrase if it is not.

passphrase.description: Optional shared passphrase used for a single private key and/or a PFX.

cert.description: Optional cert chains in PEM format. One cert chain should be provided per private key. Each cert chain should consist of the PEM formatted certificate for a provided private key, followed by the PEM formatted intermediate certificates (if any), in order, and not including the root CA (the root CA must be pre-known to the peer, see ca). When providing multiple cert chains, they do not have to be in the same order as their private keys in key. If the intermediate certificates are not provided, the peer will not be able to validate the certificate, and the handshake will fail.

ca.description: Optionally override the trusted CA certificates. Default is to trust the well-known CAs curated by Mozilla. Mozilla's CAs are completely replaced when CAs are explicitly specified using this option. The value can be a string or Buffer, or an Array of strings and/or Buffers. Any string or Buffer can contain multiple PEM CAs concatenated together. The peer's certificate must be chainable to a CA trusted by the server for the connection to be authenticated. When using certificates that are not chainable to a well-known CA, the certificate's CA must be explicitly specified as a trusted or the connection will fail to authenticate. If the peer uses a certificate that doesn't match or chain to one of the default CAs, use the ca option to provide a CA certificate that the peer's certificate can match or chain to. For self-signed certificates, the certificate is its own CA, and must be provided.

crl.description: Optional PEM formatted CRLs (Certificate Revocation Lists).

ciphers.description: Optional cipher suite specification, replacing the default. For more information, see modifying the default cipher suite.

honorCipherOrder.description: Attempt to use the server's cipher suite preferences instead of the client's. When true, causes SSL_OP_CIPHER_SERVER_PREFERENCE to be set in secureOptions, see OpenSSL Options for more information. Note: tls.createServer() sets the default value to true, other APIs that create secure contexts leave it unset.

ecdhCurve.description: A string describing a named curve to use for ECDH key agreement or false to disable ECDH. Defaults to tls.DEFAULT_ECDH_CURVE. Use crypto.getCurves() to obtain a list of available curve names. On recent releases, openssl ecparam -list_curves will also display the name and description of each available elliptic curve.

dhparam.description: Diffie Hellman parameters, required for Perfect Forward Secrecy. Use openssl dhparam to create the parameters. The key length must be greater than or equal to 1024 bits, otherwise an error will be thrown. It is strongly recommended to use 2048 bits or larger for stronger security. If omitted or invalid, the parameters are silently discarded and DHE ciphers will not be available.

secureProtocol.description: Optional SSL method to use, default is "SSLv23_method". The possible values are listed as SSL_METHODS, use the function names as strings. For example, "SSLv3_method" to force SSL version 3.

secureOptions.description: Optionally affect the OpenSSL protocol behaviour, which is not usually necessary. This should be used carefully if at all! Value is a numeric bitmask of the SSL_OP_* options from OpenSSL Options.

sessionIdContext.description: Optional opaque identifier used by servers to ensure session state is not shared between applications. Unused by clients. Note: tls.createServer() uses a 128 bit truncated SHA1 hash value generated from process.argv, other APIs that create secure contexts have no default value.
